html:
A Pentecostal church in Seoul, South Korea, founded in 1958 by the preacher David Yonggi Cho and Choi Ja-shil. It began in a tent in a poor district of a city still scarred by the Korean War.

The church belongs to the Assemblies of God, a movement that grew out of revivals like the Azusa Street Revival in Los Angeles. Cho preached healing, prayer and hope of a better life, a message that fit a country rushing from poverty to wealth. In 1973 the church moved to Yeouido, an island in the Han River, and it kept growing. By the 2000s it claimed hundreds of thousands of members, the largest single congregation in the world, with services relayed to overflow halls and satellite churches.

It stands for the rapid rise of Protestant Christianity in South Korea, which followed the earlier and smaller spread of Catholicism.
